items.title: Real-world Experience With Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy in mCRPC
items.summary: This study tracks how Lutetium-177 PSMA therapy (brand name Pluvicto) affects quality of life in real-world patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial is actively recruiting and will follow patients through treatment and after their cancer progresses. This therapy is already FDA-approved and targets PSMA-positive tumors using radioactive treatment.

items.title: Abiraterone, Olaparib, or Combined Treatment for DNA Repair Defect mCRPC
items.summary: Phase 2 trial comparing three approaches in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with DNA repair mutations: abiraterone plus prednisone alone, olaparib alone, or both combined. The trial focuses on patients with ATM, BRCA1, or BRCA2 mutations and is no longer recruiting new participants. Results could inform treatment choices for patients with these specific genetic changes.

items.title: Post-Marketing Study of Pluvicto in Korea
items.summary: This is a post-approval monitoring study of Pluvicto (Lutetium-177 PSMA therapy) being conducted in Korea. The study tracks how the already-approved radioactive treatment performs in routine clinical practice. It is currently recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

items.title: Lutetium-177 PSMA Plus Liver-Directed Therapy for mCRPC Liver Metastases
items.summary: Phase 1 safety study combining PSMA-targeted radioactive therapy (Lu-177-PSMA-617) with liver-directed treatments for patients whose prostate cancer has spread to the liver. This trial is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant disease who have failed at least one hormonal therapy. The approach aims to better control liver metastases.

items.title: CAR T-Cell Therapy Trial for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: First-in-human Phase 1 trial of A-CAR032, a CAR T-cell immunotherapy for patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed after hormonal treatments. This experimental approach genetically modifies a patient's own immune cells to attack cancer. The trial is recruiting and will assess safety and early signs of effectiveness.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Combinations for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Phase 1/2 study testing ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate, either alone or combined with other treatments for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial is recruiting patients and will measure PSA response, safety, and recommended dosing. This represents a novel targeted therapy approach.

items.title: AMG 509 Study for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Phase 1 trial evaluating AMG 509 alone and combined with abiraterone or enzalutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and focuses on safety, drug levels in the body, and early effectiveness. Parts of the trial are testing combinations with standard hormonal therapies.

items.title: TD001 Antibody-Drug Conjugate Trial for PSMA-Positive Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Phase 1/2 study of TD001, an antibody-drug conjugate targeting PSMA in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial is recruiting and will evaluate safety, drug levels, and early anti-tumor activity. This represents another targeted approach using PSMA as the target for drug delivery.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Versus Chemotherapy for mCRPC
items.summary: Large Phase 3 trial comparing ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd) to standard chemotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and measures whether patients live longer overall and longer without cancer progression compared to chemotherapy. This is a pivotal trial that could lead to FDA approval if successful.

items.title: TRC003 PSMA-Targeted Therapy Trial for Progressive mCRPC
items.summary: Phase 1/2 study of TRC003 injection in patients with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who previously received hormonal therapy or chemotherapy. The trial is recruiting 90 patients across three dose levels and will evaluate safety and effectiveness over six treatment cycles.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide for mCSPC
items.summary: Large Phase 3 trial testing whether adding the investigational drug mevrometostat to enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer. The study is recruiting patients who have not yet received androgen receptor pathway inhibitors or chemotherapy. This represents a potential new combination therapy approach.

items.title: INR731 Safety Study for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Phase 1 trial evaluating the safety and dosing of oral drug INR731, alone or combined with standard hormonal therapies, in metastatic prostate cancer patients. The study is recruiting and will measure drug levels, side effects, and early signs of anti-tumor activity. This is an early-stage investigation of a novel mechanism.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: AZD2265 Versus Standard Care for PSMA-Positive mCRPC
items.summary: Large Phase 3 trial comparing AZD2265 to standard treatments in PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and measures time to cancer progression and overall survival. This trial could establish a new treatment option if AZD2265 proves superior to current standards.

items.title: IL-12 Enhanced Human PSMA CAR T-Cells for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Research study developing an improved CAR T-cell therapy targeting PSMA for advanced prostate cancer. The approach uses a human-derived antibody fragment and adds IL-12 to enhance the immune response. Laboratory studies show increased T-cell expansion and tumor killing compared to earlier designs, suggesting potential for improved safety and effectiveness.

items.title: Top Advances in Radiopharmaceutical Therapy for Prostate Cancer in 2025
items.summary: Review article summarizing major 2025 advances in radiopharmaceutical therapy for prostate cancer. The field has evolved from pain management with radium-223 to cancer-directed treatment with PSMA-targeted therapies. The article discusses the approval and expansion of PSMA-targeted imaging and therapy as significant recent developments.

items.title: AI-Identified Biomarkers Predict Hormone Therapy Response in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Study using artificial intelligence to identify 13 cellular markers in prostate biopsy samples that predict response to neoadjuvant hormone therapy plus enzalutamide. The markers accurately identified patients who would respond to treatment and also predicted biochemical recurrence after surgery. For non-responders, the study found mTOR pathway targeting may be effective, suggesting a personalized treatment approach.

items.title: Optimizing Care for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Patients
items.source: American Society of Clinical Oncology educational book. American Society of Clinical Oncology. Annual Meeting
items.summary: Clinical practice guideline summarizing the evolving treatment landscape for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The article proposes a practical framework for treatment decisions integrating clinical features, molecular testing, imaging, and supportive care. It addresses the complexity of treatment sequencing given earlier treatment intensification and heterogeneous disease presentations.

items.title: Novel Therapies Beyond Hormone Blockade for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Comprehensive review of new treatment strategies for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer beyond standard hormone therapies. Discusses PARP inhibitors for DNA repair defects, targeted therapies for PTEN loss, PSMA radioligand therapy, bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, and immune checkpoint inhibitors. Also covers liquid biopsy and PSMA PET imaging for treatment selection.

items.title: Prognostic Factors for PSMA Radioligand Therapy in mCRPC
items.summary: Meta-analysis identifying factors that predict outcomes in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients receiving PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy. The study synthesized data on clinical, blood test, and imaging characteristics that predict progression-free and overall survival. This information helps doctors identify which patients are most likely to benefit from PSMA therapy.

items.title: PSA Decline Predicts Outcomes in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Study of 352 patients examining how PSA levels during treatment predict outcomes in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer treated with upfront combination therapy. Achieving a PSA nadir below 0.02 and a PSA decline of 99% or more were strongly associated with longer time to castration resistance and overall survival, helping identify patients with better prognosis.

items.title: Circulating Tumor DNA Predicts Survival in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Meta-analysis of 18,575 patients showing that detectable circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in blood tests predicts worse progression-free and overall survival in metastatic prostate cancer. Higher ctDNA levels and specific gene mutations detected in ctDNA were associated with poorer outcomes. This liquid biopsy approach offers a minimally invasive way to assess prognosis.

items.title: Reducing Androgen Suppression Side Effects in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Review article discussing strategies to minimize or avoid androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer while maintaining effectiveness. Recent studies show that adding androgen receptor pathway inhibitors to ADT improves survival, and research is exploring whether similar benefits can be achieved with less ADT to reduce side effects like cardiovascular disease, bone loss, and cognitive problems.

items.title: Cabazitaxel Versus Hormone Therapy After Docetaxel and Hormone Failure
items.summary: Real-world study of 517 heavily pretreated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients comparing outcomes with cabazitaxel chemotherapy versus switching to a different hormonal therapy after both docetaxel and prior hormone therapy failed. The study provides survival data to help guide treatment decisions in this challenging patient population with limited options.
